record.paper_title: Some open problems and research directions in the mathematical study of fluid dynamics.
record.context_brief: Inertial manifolds for forced two-dimensional Navier-Stokes
record.original_question: For the two-dimensional spatially periodic Navier-Stokes equations forced by a time-independent force, all solutions converge as time tends to infinity to a compact global attractor A of finite Hausdorff dimension. Are the dynamics on this attractor conjugate to a finite-dimensional smooth dynamical system, with the remaining infinitely many degrees of freedom transient in a controllable way, or equivalently does an inertial manifold or consistent finite-dimensional parametrization capture the global long-time behavior?

evidence.quote: This is the question of inertial manifolds, as open now as it was when it was born

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the two-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations on the torus $\mathbb{T}^2 = \mathbb{R}^2/\mathbb{Z}^2$,
$$\partial_t u + (u\cdot\nabla)u - \nu \Delta u + \nabla p = f, \qquad \nabla\cdot u = 0,$$
with periodic boundary conditions, viscosity $\nu>0$, zero spatial mean, and a time-independent forcing $f \in L^2(\mathbb{T}^2)^2$ with zero mean. It is known that this dynamical system, viewed on the phase space $H = \{u\in L^2(\mathbb{T}^2)^2 : \nabla\cdot u=0,\ \int u =0\}$, possesses a compact global attractor $\mathcal{A}\subset H$ of finite Hausdorff (and fractal) dimension which attracts every trajectory as $t\to\infty$.

An inertial manifold for this system is a finite-dimensional smooth (at least $C^1$) Lipschitz manifold $\mathcal{M}\subset H$ that is (i) positively invariant under the semiflow, (ii) contains the global attractor $\mathcal{A}$, and (iii) attracts every trajectory exponentially fast (the exponential tracking property): for every $u_0\in H$ there exist $v_0\in\mathcal{M}$ and constants $C,\kappa>0$ such that $\|S(t)u_0 - S(t)v_0\|_H \le C e^{-\kappa t}$ for all $t\ge 0$, where $S(t)$ denotes the solution semigroup.

Question: Does there exist an inertial manifold $\mathcal{M}$ for the two-dimensional periodic Navier–Stokes equations as above? Equivalently, is the long-time dynamics on $\mathcal{A}$ conjugate (via a smooth finite-dimensional reduction with exponentially decaying transient infinite-dimensional modes) to a finite-dimensional smooth dynamical system?
artifact.status_search_result: The existence (or nonexistence) of an inertial manifold for the two-dimensional periodic Navier–Stokes equations remains a well-known open problem. Partial progress exists for modified models (hyperviscous Navier–Stokes, Leray-α type models) and through approximate inertial manifolds, but the standard 2D Navier–Stokes case is unresolved because the spectral gap condition is not known to hold.

status_evidence.title: Inertial manifolds for the two-dimensional hyperviscous Navier-Stokes equations
status_evidence.snippet: the existence or non-existence of an IM for 2D Navier–Stokes remains an open problem
status_evidence.claim: The existence of inertial manifolds for 2D Navier–Stokes is open; progress is restricted to hyperviscous variants.

status_evidence.title: Approximate inertial manifolds for 2D Navier-Stokes equations
status_evidence.snippet: it is still an open problem for the existence of the inertial manifolds for Navier-Stokes equations
status_evidence.claim: Only approximate inertial manifolds are constructed; existence of true IM remains open.
